modern_osis:
Original heading

Solomon's choice of wisdom, His strength and wealth.

Solomon seeks wisdom

Solomon began his reign by visiting God's altar publicly and reverently.

People who eagerly pursue present and earthly things are likely to be disappointed.

Those who entrust their circumstances to God's providence may not possess the most, but they enjoy the greatest comfort in what they have.

Those who make this world their ultimate goal fail to obtain the next world, and are disappointed with this one as well.

Those who aim instead for the world to come will receive it, with complete satisfaction; meanwhile they will also receive as much of this world's goods as is truly good for them along the way.

Let us therefore be content without the impressive things that people usually covet, since those things often become deadly traps for the soul.
classic_reading:
[2Chr.1.1]
2 Chronicles
Solomon's choice of wisdom, His strength and wealth.
--SOLOMON began his reign with a pious, public visit to God's altar. Those that pursue present things most eagerly, are likely to be disappointed; while those that refer themselves to the providence of God, if they have not the most, have the most comfort. Those that make this world their end, come short of the other, and are disappointed in this also; but those that make the other world their end, shall not only obtain that, and full satisfaction in it, but shall have as much of this world as is good for them, in their way. Let us then be contented, without those great things which men generally covet, but which commonly prove fatal snares to the soul.

modern_osis:
Original heading

Solomon's message to Huram respecting the temple, His treaty with Huram.

Solomon sends to Huram concerning the temple

Solomon told Huram about the particular services that would be performed in God's temple.

Unlike the mysteries of pagan superstition, the truths and mysteries of genuine faith do not need to be concealed.

Solomon wanted Huram to form great and exalted thoughts of the God of Israel.

We likewise should not be fearful or ashamed of any opportunity to speak about God and impress others with the importance of his favor and service.

While Israel remained faithful to God's law and worship, neighboring nations were willing to learn true religion from the Israelites.

Earlier, when Israel had turned from the Lord, the people had willingly absorbed the superstition and idolatry of neighboring nations.

A wise and godly king is evidence of God's special love for his people.

How much greater was that love when God gave his only Son to believing people as their Prince and Savior!
classic_reading:
[2Chr.2.1]
Chapter 2
Solomon's message to Huram respecting the temple, His treaty with Huram.
--Solomon informs Huram of the particular services to be performed in the temple. The mysteries of the true religion, unlike those of the Gentile superstitions, sought not concealment. Solomon endeavoured to possess Huram with great and high thoughts of the God of Israel. We should not be afraid or ashamed to embrace every opportunity to speak of God, and to impress others with a deep sense of the importance of his favour and service. Now that the people of Israel kept close to the law and worship of God, the neighbouring nations were willing to be taught by them in the true religion, as the Israelites had been willing in the days of their apostacy, to be infected with the idolatries and superstitions of their neighbours. A wise and pious king is an evidence of the Lord's special love for his people. How great then was God's love to his believing people, in giving his only-begotten Son to be their Prince and their Saviour.

modern_osis:
Original heading

The building of the temple.

The temple is constructed

The building of the temple is described more fully in 1 Kings 6.

It had to be built on the ground David had prepared: not merely land he purchased, but the place he selected by God's direction.

Clear instructions allow us to begin work with confidence and continue it with peace.

Blessed be God, the Scriptures thoroughly equip his people for every good work.

Let us search the Bible daily, praying that the Lord will enable us to understand, believe and obey his word.

Then our path and work will become clear, and everything can be begun, continued and completed in him.

As we contemplate God through Jesus Christ, his true Temple, far more glorious than Solomon's, may we ourselves be formed into a spiritual house, a dwelling place of God through the Spirit.
classic_reading:
[2Chr.3.1]
Chapter 3
The building of the temple.
--There is a more particular account of the building of the temple in 1Ki 6. It must be in the place David had prepared, not only which he had purchased, but which he had fixed on by Divine direction. Full instructions enable us to go about our work with certainty and to proceed therein with comfort. Blessed be God, the Scriptures are enough to render the man of God thoroughly furnished for every good work. Let us search the Scriptures daily, beseeching the Lord to enable us to understand, believe, and obey his word, that our work and our way may be made plain, and that all may be begun, continued, and ended in him. Beholding God, in Christ, his true Temple, more glorious than that of Solomon's, may we become a spiritual house, a habitation of God through the Spirit.

modern_osis:
Original heading

The furniture of the temple.

The temple's furnishings

This chapter further describes the furnishings of God's house.

Both outside and inside, the objects pictured gospel grace and pointed toward good things still to come, whose substance is Jesus Christ.

The bronze altar appears here, though the account of its construction was not included in Kings.

Every sacrifice was offered upon it, and it sanctified the gift.

People worshiping in the courts could see the sacrifices burning.

That sight might lead them to consider the great Sacrifice who would come in the fullness of time to take away sin and end death—something the blood of bulls and goats could never accomplish.

As the smoke rose, they could direct their own hearts to heaven in holy longing for God and his favor.

In all our worship, the eye of faith should remain fixed on Christ.

The temple contained more furnishings than the tabernacle had done.

This pictured the future enlargement of God's church and multiplication of worshipers.

Blessed be God, there is enough in Christ for every one of them.
classic_reading:
[2Chr.4.1]
Chapter 4
The furniture of the temple.
--Here is a further account of the furniture of God's house. Both without doors and within, there was that which typified the grace of the gospel, and shadowed out good things to come, of which the substance is Christ. There was the brazen altar. The making of this was not mentioned in the book of Kings. On this all the sacrifices were offered, and it sanctified the gift. The people who worshipped in the courts might see the sacrifices burned. They might thus be led to consider the great Sacrifice, to be offered in the fulness of time, to take away sin, and put an end to death, which the blood of bulls and goats could not possibly do. And, with the smoke of the sacrifices, their hearts might ascend to heaven, in holy desires towards God and his favour. In all our devotions we must keep the eye of faith fixed upon Christ. The furniture of the temple, compared with that of the tabernacle, showed that God's church would be enlarged, and his worshippers multiplied. Blessed be God, there is enough in Christ for all.

modern_osis:
Original chapter outlineOriginal outlineVersesThe ark placed in the temple.1–10The temple filled with glory.11–14
The ark is placed in the temple (verses 1–10)

The ark was a picture of Christ and therefore a sign of God's presence.

Jesus has promised to be with his followers always, even to the end of the world.

When we claim that promise through faith and prayer, its effect is as though the ark itself were brought into our worship gatherings.

We should seek that presence earnestly.

When Christ is formed within a person, God's law is written upon the heart.

The ark of the covenant has, in that sense, been established there.

The soul becomes a temple of the Holy Spirit, and finds genuine satisfaction.

God's glory fills the temple (verses 11–14)

God took possession of the building by filling it with a cloud.

This showed that he accepted the temple as he had accepted Moses' tabernacle and assured his people that he would continue to be the same gracious God to them.

If we want God to dwell in our hearts, we must make room for him: everything else must yield.

The Word became flesh.

When he comes to his temple like a refiner's fire, who can endure the day of his coming?

May he prepare us for that day.
classic_reading:
[2Chr.5.1-2Chr.5.10]
Chapter 5
Chapter Outline
The ark placed in the temple. | (1-10) |
The temple filled with glory. | (11-14) |
Verses 1-10
The ark was a type of Christ, and, as such, a token of the presence of God. That gracious promise, Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world, does, in effect, bring the ark into our religious assemblies, if we by faith and prayer plead that promise; and this we should be most earnest for. When Christ is formed in a soul, the law written in the heart, the ark of the covenant settled there, so that it becomes the temple of the Holy Ghost, there is true satisfaction in that soul.
[2Chr.5.11-2Chr.5.14]
Verses 11-14
God took possession of the temple; he filled it with a cloud. Thus he signified his acceptance of this temple, to be the same to him that the tabernacle of Moses was, and assured his people that he would be the same in it. Would we have God dwell in our hearts, we must leave room for him; every thing else must give way. The Word was made flesh; and when he comes to his temple, like a refiner's fire, who may abide the day of his coming? May he prepare us for that day.

modern_osis:
Original heading

Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple.

Solomon prays at the dedication

Notice the order of Solomon's prayer.

First, and most importantly, he asks for repentance and forgiveness. This is the greatest blessing and the only secure foundation for other acts of mercy.

Only afterward does he pray for temporal benefits.

In this way Solomon teaches us what we should value and seek most earnestly in our prayers.

Jesus Christ teaches the same thing in his perfect pattern of prayer: only one request concerns outward needs, while the others concern spiritual blessings.

The temple pictured the human nature of Christ, in whom all the fullness of deity dwells bodily.

The ark pictured his obedience and suffering, through which repentant sinners receive access to God reconciled to them and enjoy fellowship with him.

In the person of Emmanuel, Jehovah has made our human nature his permanent dwelling place. Through him he dwells among his church of redeemed sinners and delights in them.

May our hearts become his dwelling place.

May Christ live in them by faith, making them temples dedicated to him and pouring his love into them.

May the Father look upon us through his Anointed One, remember us and bless us according to his mercy toward sinners through Jesus Christ.
classic_reading:
[2Chr.6.1]
Chapter 6
Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple.
--The order of Solomon's prayer is to be observed. First and chiefly, he prays for repentance and forgiveness, which is the chief blessing, and the only solid foundation of other mercies: he then prays for temporal mercies; thereby teaching us what things to mind and desire most in our prayers. This also Christ hath taught us in his perfect pattern and form of prayer, where there is but one prayer for outward, and all the rest are for spiritual blessings. The temple typified the human nature of Christ, in whom dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. The ark typified his obedience and sufferings, by which repenting sinners have access to a reconciled God, and communion with him. Jehovah has made our nature his resting-place for ever, in the person of Emmanuel, and through him he dwells with, and delights in his church of redeemed sinners. May our hearts become his resting-place; may Christ dwell therein by faith, consecrating them as his temples, and shedding abroad his love therein. May the Father look upon us in and through his Anointed; and may he remember and bless us in all things, according to his mercy to sinners, in and through Christ.

modern_osis:
Original heading

God's answer to Solomon's prayer.

God answers Solomon

God graciously answered Solomon's prayer.

His mercy toward sinners was shown in a way that impressed all who received it with his majesty and holiness.

The people worshiped and praised him.

When God reveals himself as a consuming fire to sinners, his people can rejoice in him as their light.

Indeed, they had good reason to say he was good in doing this.

It is because of God's mercy that we ourselves are not consumed. Instead, a sacrifice was offered on our behalf, for which we should be deeply thankful.

Anyone who truly looks in faith upon the Savior suffering and dying for human sin will experience deeper godly sorrow, greater hatred of sin, closer watchfulness and a holier life.

Solomon successfully completed his plans for beautifying God's house and his own.

People who begin by serving God are likely to prosper in their other responsibilities.

It was to Solomon's credit that he completed what he undertook, though it was God's grace that made his success possible.

Let us reverence God and not sin.

Let us fear his displeasure, hope in his mercy and walk according to his commands.
classic_reading:
[2Chr.7.1]
Chapter 7
God's answer to Solomon's prayer.
--God gave a gracious answer to Solomon's prayer. The mercies of God to sinners are made known in a manner well suited to impress all who receive them, with his majesty and holiness. The people worshipped and praised God. When he manifests himself as a consuming Fire to sinners, his people can rejoice in him as their Light. Nay, they had reason to say, that God was good in this. It is of the Lord's mercies we are not consumed, but the sacrifice in our stead, for which we should be very thankful. And whoever beholds with true faith, the Saviour agonizing and dying for man's sin, will, by that view, find his godly sorrow enlarged, his hatred of sin increased, his soul made more watchful, and his life more holy. Solomon prosperously effected all he designed, for adorning both God's house and his own. Those who begin with the service of God, are likely to go on successfully in their own affairs. It was Solomon's praise, that what he undertook, he went through with; it was by the grace of God that he prospered in it. Let us then stand in awe, and sin not. Let us fear the Lord's displeasure, hope in his mercy, and walk in his commandments.

modern_osis:
Original heading

Solomon's buildings and trade.

Solomon's works, worship and trade

Governing a family in the fear of God sometimes requires more wisdom and determination than governing a kingdom with honor.

That task becomes harder when one's spouse is a hindrance rather than a fitting helper.

Solomon maintained the appointed sacrifices according to Moses' law.

Building the altar and seeing fire descend from heaven would have been useless if sacrifices were not then continually brought.

We, too, are required to bring spiritual sacrifices every day and every week.

A settled pattern of devotion is good.

When temple service had been properly organized, the house of the Lord was said to be complete.

The work of worship, not merely the building, was the essential matter.

The temple was not truly finished until those duties were established.

Canaan was a rich land, yet its people needed to obtain gold from Ophir.

Israel was a wise nation, yet relied on the king of Tyre's sailors for expertise at sea.

Grace is better wealth than gold, and knowledge of God and his law is better than worldly expertise.

Let the children of this world struggle over its toys.

As God's children, let us store treasure in heaven, because our hearts will follow what we treasure.
classic_reading:
[2Chr.8.1]
Chapter 8
Solomon's buildings and trade.
--It sometimes requires more wisdom and resolution to govern a family in the fear of God, than to govern a kingdom with reputation. The difficulty is increased, when a man has a hinderance instead of a help meet in the wife of his bosom. Solomon kept up the holy sacrifices, according to the law of Moses. In vain had the altar been built, in vain had fire come down from heaven, if sacrifices had not been constantly brought. Spiritual sacrifices are required of us, which we are to bring daily and weekly; it is good to be in a settled method of devotion. When the service of the temple was put into good order, it is said, The house of the Lord was perfected. The work was the main matter, not the place; the temple was unfinished till all this was done. Canaan was a rich country, and yet must send to Ophir for gold The Israelites were a wise people, but must be beholden to the king of Tyre for men that had knowledge of the seas. Grace, and not gold, is the best riches, and acquaintance with God and his law, the best knowledge. Leaving the children of this world to scramble for the toys of this world, may we, as the children of God, lay up our treasure in heaven, that where our treasure is, our hearts also may be.

modern_osis:
Original chapter outlineOriginal outlineVersesThe queen of Sheba.1–12Solomon's riches, and his death.13–31
The queen of Sheba (verses 1–12)

This story has already been considered in 1 Kings 10.

Yet our Savior used the queen of Sheba as an example of someone who earnestly sought him (Matthew 12:42).

We should not pass over the lesson.

People who know the value of genuine wisdom will begrudge no expense or difficulty involved in obtaining it.

The queen traveled far and spent much to hear Solomon's wisdom.

She learned from him to serve God and fulfill her duty, and believed that knowledge more than repaid her effort.

Heavenly wisdom is the pearl of great price.

Even if we surrender everything to receive it, we make a good bargain.

Solomon's wealth and death (verses 13–31)

The imported objects listed here suggest that prosperity had led Solomon and his people to value things that were rare and interesting but not useful in themselves.

True wisdom and happiness always belong together.

There is no similar necessary connection between wealth and enjoyment of this life.

Let us draw near to the Savior to find rest for our souls.

Solomon ruled with unprecedented wealth, power, ease and abundance.

He reigned in profound peace for forty years, unlike the great kings chiefly remembered for warfare.

God fulfilled his promise to give him riches and honor beyond those of other kings.

His splendor was a faint image of the spiritual glory of Messiah's kingdom, whose throne stands above every throne.

Yet Solomon died and left all his wealth and power to a successor whom he knew would act foolishly (Ecclesiastes 2:18–19).

That was vanity and vexation of spirit.

Neither power, riches nor wisdom can prevent death or prepare the soul for it.

But thanks be to God: through Jesus Christ our Lord, he gives the true believer victory even over that dreaded enemy.
classic_reading:
[2Chr.9.1-2Chr.9.12]
Chapter 9
Chapter Outline
The queen of Sheba. | (1-12) |
Solomon's riches, and his death. | (13-31) |
Verses 1-12
This history has been considered, 1Ki 10; yet because our Saviour has proposed it as an example in seeking after him, [Matt.12.42] Mt 12:42, we must not pass it over without observing, that those who know the worth of true wisdom will grudge no pains or cost to obtain it. The queen of Sheba put herself to a great deal of trouble and expense to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and yet, learning from him to serve God, and do her duty, she thought herself well paid for her pains. Heavenly wisdom is that pearl of great price, for which, if we part with all, we make a good bargain.
[2Chr.9.13-2Chr.9.31]
Verses 13-31
The imports here mentioned, would show that prosperity drew the minds of Solomon and his subjects to the love of things curious and uncommon, though useless in themselves. True wisdom and happiness are always united together; but no such alliance exists between wealth and the enjoyment of the things of this life. Let us then acquaint ourselves with the Saviour, that we may find rest for our souls. Here is Solomon reigning in wealth and power, in ease and fulness, the like of which could never since be found; for the most known of the great princes of the earth were famed for their wars; whereas Solomon reigned forty years in profound peace. The promise was fulfilled, that God would give him riches and honour, such as no kings have had or shall have. The lustre wherein he appeared, was typical of the spiritual glory of the kingdom of the Messiah, and but a faint representation of His throne, which is above every throne. Here is Solomon dying, and leaving all his wealth and power to one who he knew would be a fool! [Eccl.2.18] Ec 2:18, 19. This was not only vanity, but vexation of spirit. Neither power, wealth, nor wisdom, can ward off or prepare for the stroke of death. But thanks be to God who giveth the victory to the true believer, even over this dreaded enemy, through Jesus Christ our Lord.

modern_osis:
Original heading

The ten tribes revolt from Rehoboam.

The division of the kingdom

Moderate and reasonable counsel is usually the wisest and best.

Gentleness can accomplish what force and harshness cannot.

Most people respond better to words spoken kindly.

Good words cost us only a little self-denial, yet they may accomplish a great deal.

To ruin people, it is often enough merely to leave them under the rule of their own pride and anger.

Yet whatever human beings plan, God continues accomplishing his purposes through everything and fulfilling the word he has spoken.

No one can pass on wisdom or prosperity as an inheritance to children by simply choosing to do so.

Nevertheless, our conduct—whether good or bad—usually affects those who come after us.

Therefore, let us pursue the good things that will belong to us forever.

Let us seek God's blessing for our children and their descendants rather than wealth or worldly promotion.
classic_reading:
[2Chr.10.1]
Chapter 10
The ten tribes revolt from Rehoboam.
--Moderate counsels are wisest and best. Gentleness will do what violence will not do. Most people like to be accosted mildly. Good words cost only a little self-denial, yet they purchase great things. No more needs to be done to ruin men, than to leave them to their own pride and passion. Thus, whatever are the devices of men, God is doing his own work by all, and fulfilling the word which he has spoken. No man can bequeath his prosperity to his heirs any more than his wisdom; though our children will generally be affected by our conduct, whether good or bad. Let us then seek those good things which will be our own for ever; and crave the blessing of God upon our posterity, in preference to wealth or worldly exaltation.
